title: Add Event Trellis dashboard and token-cost fallback suggester
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Adds an 'Event Trellis' small-multiples dashboard, implements a lightweight token-cost fallback suggester service that annotates traces with candidate fallback model hints, and wires kernel warmup logs into invocation trace links. Motivation: production customers were hitting unexpected token-cost spikes during specific event types (batch ingestion, conversational streaming handoffs). Existing dashboards show per-route aggregates but make it hard to visually compare behavior across event types and warmup epochs. This change provides: 1) a trellis view (rows=event type, columns=hour buckets) showing median/95p token cost, median latency, and kernel-warmup-signal sparklines; 2) a background suggester that runs in the observability ingest path to attach recommended fallback variants when per-invocation token-cost exceeds a configurable threshold; 3) trace enrichment to attach the most-recent kernel warmup log pointer for quick debugging. Checklist: - [x] Trellis dashboard JSON and panels - [x] small backend service: observability/fallback_suggester.py - [x] trace enrichment in span-enricher.go - [x] docs: docs/observability/event_trellis.md - [x] unit tests for suggester heuristic - [x] e2e smoke run against staging dashboards

Commits (high-level): - 9bd3f2c: add dashboard definition and test fixtures - c4a7b0e: implement suggester service and configuration - f1e5a12: span enrichment: attach warmup-log link & fallback hint - ab7d55f: add dashboard docs and runbook section - 3c9a0d1: unit + integration tests; lint fixes

Changed areas (high level): - webapp/dashboards/event_trellis.json: new dashboard with 12 panels (median token cost, 95p token cost, median latency, kernel-warmup-sparkline). - observability/fallback_suggester.py: a small async service that inspects incoming metric envelopes and emits a lightweight annotation to the trace store when trigger conditions are met. - rpc/telemetry/span_enricher.go: enriches spans with 'fallback_hint' and 'warmup_log_url' fields when present. - docs/observability/event_trellis.md: runbook + how to interpret trellis rows/columns. - scripts/bench/warmup-replay.sh: helper for synthetic warmup logs to validate warmup linking.

Testing/CI: - Unit tests: fallback_suggester tests cover heuristic tuning and thresholding. - Integration: smoke test renders dashboard panels in staging and verifies panel queries return non-empty series. - CI checks: go vet + golangci-lint, python pytest, frontend linting. All checks passed on the final run (two flaky graphQL snapshot tests were retried and resolved).

Review conversation (selected): - Diego Ruiz (review): "Nice visualization idea. Two asks: (1) can we make the suggester idempotent and throttle annotations to avoid span spam? (2) please add a short TTL for warmup_log_url links to avoid stale pointers." - Maya Chen (author): "Addressed both: suggester now dedups on invocation id and rate-limits to 1 annotation per-invocation; warmup URLs are tombstoned after 7 days (configurable). PTAL." - Asha Patel (review): "Please add a note in the runbook for oncall about interpreting the 95p token-cost delta column and recommended mitigation steps (scale, fallback, prompt trim)." - Maya Chen: "Added runbook section and an automated quick-link in the dashboard that opens the suggester log for the selected cell." - Liam O'Connor: "Approvals pending a small nit on metric labels (use 'tokens_cost' instead of 'token_costs')." - Maya Chen: "Renamed the metric alias in the panel queries and pushed commit." - Diego Ruiz: "LGTM, tested on staging. Approving." - PR merged by Maya Chen via squash merge.

Operational notes & rollout: - Default threshold for the suggester is conservative (750 token-cost units per invocation); config is in infra/config/observability.yaml under 'fallback_suggester.threshold'. - We deliberately keep the suggester out of the main ingest hot path by running it as an async sidecar; deployment will start as 10% of observability ingestion workers for 48 hours, then scale up if no noise. - Dashboards are namespaced under 'Observability / Event Trellis' and the runbook link points to the docs page. - No schema migrations required for trace store; the enrichment is optional and stored as tags.

Release notes: - New 'Event Trellis' dashboard for rapid cross-event comparison of token-cost and latency. - Suggester annotates traces with recommended fallback model variants when token-cost spikes are detected. - Kernel warmup logs are linked in traces to speed root-cause for warmup-related latency.

notes_for_oncall: If the trellis shows recurring 95p token-cost spikes for an event type, first check fallback_suggester annotations on the upper-right cell; suggested mitigations: enable fallback variants, increase burst capacity, or apply prompt trimming. If warmup_log_url is present, open the linked log and look for kernel warmup events in the 30s before invocation.
